findings.message: Fallback printf statements constructing JSON (e.g., the router-failure and empty-response paths) substitute _rc_reason and _rc_disp via %s without JSON-escaping; if the router RC classifier ever returns a reason string containing '"' or '\', the fallback produces malformed JSON — this pattern is pre-existing (v1 used the same printf fallback) and the change extends it to new exit paths.

The new early-exit paths in _impact_run_entry write verdict:'broken', a value not declared in manifest.yaml's valid_verdicts:[complete,incomplete,error]; per issue #1708 the engine treats any verdict outside the declared set as a structural failure, so these paths would produce structural failures rather than validated-contract failures — this appears intentional (modelled after the plan plugin) but is not recorded in valid_verdicts nor in the manifest comment.

New SPEC-9 test setup constructs the ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS JSON via printf with bare %s substitution of $SCOPE_MANIFEST, $DESIGN_MD, and $PLAN_JSON paths; if a temp path contains '"' or '\' (e.g., on a runner with unusual TMPDIR), the JSON is malformed and the test silently resolves wrong paths rather than failing explicitly.

Same printf-into-JSON pattern used for the new v2 fixture setup (STATE_DIR and ARTIFACTS_DIR substituted via %s without escaping); pre-existing test fixtures use the same pattern, but this instance is newly introduced by the v2 migration.

_impact_on_signal references $STAGE_SIGNAL_DISPOSITION and $STAGE_SIGNAL_REASON without explicit :-empty guards; under set -u, if stage_signal_begin fires the callback before those variables are exported by the signal library, the handler aborts without writing the interrupted result, defeating the signal-guard contract.
